entering-the-camp.text: You tie the rope around the boulder and prepare to climb down.
You pull on the rope and miraculously, it comes loose.

hamal-s-daughter.text: If The Fremennik Trials has been completed, the player will introduce themselves with their Fremennik name, and Hamal will use that name in place of the player's username throughout the quest.

hamal-s-daughter.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
hamal-s-daughter.text: Greetings, outerlander, I am Hamal. I am the chieftain of this tribe.

hamal-s-daughter.player: And my name is [player name/Fremennik name], honourable chieftain.

hamal-s-daughter.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
hamal-s-daughter.text: So tell me what you want from us.

options.condition: If The Fremennik Trials has been completed

steps.player: Actually, I'm a Fremennik, not an outerlander.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: We are not Fremennik, outerlander.

steps.player: But you look like Fremennik!

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: And you do not look like a Fremennik, but still claim to be one.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: But I will not deceive you. We were part of the Fremennik once, but left the village of Rellekka long ago.

options.text: So what are you doing up here?

steps.player: That's fascinating, but I'm afraid I have other things to do at the moment.
Why is everyone being so hostile to me?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: We are a solitary group, outerlander, and have little experience or interest in outside contact.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: It is also our custom not to talk to outerlanders without my sanction. And I see no reason to sanction it for you.

options.text: So what are you doing up here?

steps.player: So what are you lot all doing up here in the mountains?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: We left Rellekka because we wanted to live closer to nature. We feel that the people of Rellekka have grown complacent and rely too much on their tools rather than their skill. And while they share our view on the sanctity

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: of the runestones, they still employ and actively use magic.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Their Seer is an affront to the gods!
If The Fremennik Trials has been completed:

steps.player: And you haven't even seen what he did to his house!

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Anyway.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: We do not recognise the council of Rellekka and want nothing more to do with them. We live on rock and stone now, pure and hard.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: We move on to another part of the mountain slope when the rough land cannot sustain us anymore.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: That said, we have tarried at this location for too long and should be moving on.

steps.player: So why are you still here?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: For one thing, this side of the mountain is mostly free from the menace of the trolls and the delvings of the deformed dwarves.

steps.player: And?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Well, you see...

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: My daughter has gone missing. We have been looking for her and cannot go on without her.

steps.player: A damsel in distress! I will search for her!

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Haha, you have spirit, [player name/fremennik name].

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: But we do not employ outerlanders.

steps.player: You don't need to employ me! Just let me look for her.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Hmmm.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: That seems acceptable to me. Very well, I will allow you to look for her.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: I will instruct my people to let you roam about the area freely, and give limited consent to them to talk to you.

steps.player: Great! I'll be back with her soon. Just wait here.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Oh, I'll be waiting here alright.

steps.player: I'm sorry to hear that.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: We do not need your sympathy, outerlander.

steps.player: Maybe the trolls got her?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Do not say such things in jest, outerlander.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Besides, stealth and kidnapping is not their way.

steps.player: Forget it then, you can figure it out on your own.

options.text: Oh, I'll stop talking to you then.

steps.player: Oh, I'll stop talking to you then.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: As you wish, outerlander.

steps.player: I'm looking for a quest! Do you have any for me?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: We do not employ outerlanders.

steps.player: Okay, I know the drill, where do I sign up for the trials to join your tribe?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: And we certainly don't let them join us!

options.text: Any idea on where I should start looking?

steps.player: Uhm... any idea on where I should start looking for your daughter?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: There is a large pool of water beyond the camp. She used to go there often, it was her favourite spot.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Ragnar, her fiance, is probably there as well. I will give him my permission to talk to you.

options.text: What does your daughter look like?

steps.player: What does your daughter look like?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: She is the fairest maiden of all our tribe, and I daresay of all the northern lands. She has flowing black hair, and when last we saw her, she was wearing a brown dress.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Perhaps you should speak to the man she is to marry, tribesman Ragnar. He can probably tell you more.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: You can find him out by the pool beyond the camp, where my daughter used to go so often.

crisis-camp-dwellers.text: Depending on which camp dweller is spoken to, different dialogue is given.

steps.player: Hello! I'm trying to help your chieftain here.

steps.speaker: Camp dweller
steps.text: We don't need any help.

steps.player: Hello there! Can you help me?

steps.text: The camp dweller shakes his head.

steps.speaker: Camp dweller
steps.text: Stay away from me, outerlander.

steps.player: I think I need some help.
Well, yes...

steps.speaker: Camp dweller
steps.text: Run along then!

steps.player: Hello, I'm-

steps.speaker: Camp dweller
steps.text: No.

steps.player: What?
But I-
Isn't there-
Never mind.

crisis-guard-by-the-entrance.player: Can you come and help me? The chieftain's daughter-

crisis-guard-by-the-entrance.speaker: Guard
crisis-guard-by-the-entrance.text: No, outerlander, I'm guarding this mountain pass from trolls and inquisitive people like you.

crisis-guard-by-the-entrance.player: Doesn't look like you were very successful in the last regard.

crisis-guard-by-the-entrance.speaker: Guard
crisis-guard-by-the-entrance.text: If the chieftain would let me, I would correct that oversight.

crisis-jokul.player: Do you have any idea where the chieftain's daughter is?

crisis-jokul.speaker: Jokul
crisis-jokul.text: That's what we would all like to know.

crisis-ragnar.speaker: Ragnar
crisis-ragnar.text: So, you are the outerlander whom Hamal said would look for Asleif.

crisis-ragnar.speaker: Ragnar
crisis-ragnar.text: You don't even know her name!

crisis-ragnar.speaker: Ragnar
crisis-ragnar.text: I am sorry outerlander, I have not spoken with your kind for a long time and I'm not feeling so well. You see, I was set to marry Asleif, the most beautiful woman ever to grace this world.

options.text: Do you have any idea where she might be?

steps.player: Do you have any idea where she might be?

steps.speaker: Ragnar
steps.text: She used to come here every day, you know, whenever our camp was set up in the vicinity. She would come to sing, her voice reflecting on the mountains and falling into the pool like sparkling silver. Sometimes I think I can hear her singing, but when I follow the sound around the pool I just end up here again.

steps.player: So... do you have any idea where she might be now?

steps.speaker: Ragnar
steps.text: We were supposed to meet here, at the tree by the pool. I think if I wait long enough maybe she will show up again.

steps.player: But... you don't actually have any idea where she is right at the moment?

steps.speaker: Ragnar
steps.text: If I knew I wouldn't be standing here, would I?

options.text: What do you mean, my kind?

steps.text: Before The Fremennik Trials:

steps.player: What do you mean, my kind?

steps.speaker: Ragnar
steps.text: You outerlanders with your fancy armour and your runestones and all your convenient little tools.

steps.player: Oh, that kind...

steps.text: After The Fremennik Trials:

steps.player: What do you mean, my kind? I'm a Fremennik you know.

steps.speaker: Ragnar
steps.text: Yet you still use magic, I assume, and have little actual knowledge of the earth and the rock that you stand on every day.

steps.player: I suppose...

steps.speaker: Ragnar
steps.text: Then you are an ignorant, an insult to the gods... and an outerlander.

steps.player: Okay, okay, you made your point!

crisis-the-shining-pool-listening-to-the.text: You think you can hear soft singing!
The sound seems to be coming from the center of the pool.

crisis-the-shining-pool-attempting-to-cl.text: The bark has become slippery with water, you fail to find a suitable hold.
Perhaps you could find something to apply to it to make it less slippery.

crisis-the-shining-pool-gathering-the-mu.text: You dig up some mud with your bare hands. Yuck, now they're all sticky.

crisis-using-the-mud-on-the-tree.text: Great, now the tree bar isn't slippery anymore!

crisis-using-the-mud-on-the-tree-climbin.text: You jump up to grab the bark of the tree...
...and jump down to the little island!

crisis-using-the-mud-on-the-tree-jumping.text: If the player doesn't use the broken staff:

steps.text: That would be a good idea... if the pole wasn't broken, that is.

crisis-using-the-mud-on-the-tree-jumping.text: If the player uses an appropriate staff:

steps.text: You plant your staff into the clump of rocks...
...then successfully jump across!

crisis-using-the-mud-on-the-tree-jumping.text: If the player doesn't use an appropriate staff:

steps.text: You slip and fall into the water!
You only just manage to get to shore!

crisis-using-the-mud-on-the-tree-using-t.text: If the player uses a plank:

steps.text: You place the plank on the two flat stones...
...then successfully walk across!

crisis-using-the-mud-on-the-tree-using-t.text: If the player doesn't use a plank:

steps.text: You slip and fall into the water!
You only just manage to get to shore!

crisis-using-the-mud-on-the-tree-listeni.text: You can clearly hear the voice coming from the water now.
'Listen to me, [player name/fremennik name], listen to what I will say.'

steps.player: I think I'm going mad, I'm starting to hear things.
Hello! Who are you? And where for that matter?

steps.text: 'I am all around you. I am the soft singing in the wind. I am the faint rippling of the water. I am the stone of the rocks around you.'

steps.player: Well, I suppose that answered both questions then.

steps.text: 'I am the voice of Asleif, daughter of Hamal, son of Wulfgard.'

steps.player: Wait, you're Asleif? I think I was looking for you! Where are you hiding?

steps.text: 'Asleif is no longer in your world, she dwells in the halls of her ancestors now.'

steps.player: But I thought you said you were Asleif?

steps.text: 'I am but the voice of her, an echo of the past, reflected on the water. A tiny part of her spirit.'

options.text: I think I'd better have a lie down.

steps.player: I think I'd better have a lie down, I'm starting to get a little dizzy.

options.text: So what exactly do you want from me?

steps.player: So what exactly do you want from me?

steps.text: 'I am greatly concerned for the people who were once my tribesmen. You must help me, [player name/fremennik name], for their current course will lead to their doom.'

steps.player: Er, I don't think they like the idea of me helping them.

steps.text: 'Listen to me, and judge then if you think yourself capable or not.'
'Our tribesmen are the children of the Fremennik of Rellekka. The parting was a bitter affair and the two groups never forgave each other.'
'I ask you, [player name/fremennik name], to help bring these two people closer together again.'

options.text: That sounds like something I can do.

steps.player: All right, that sounds like something I can do.

steps.text: 'There is another thing, [player name/fremennik name], that I ask of you.'

steps.player: Yes?

steps.text: 'My father has not moved camp for far too long. There is very little food now for my people. You must find a new supply of food for them, for I fear the worst.'

steps.player: I'll get right on it.
So let's see, peace with Rellekka, and a new supply of food.'

steps.text: 'Thank you, [player name/fremennik name], and may the gods bless you on your journey.'

steps.player: I'm sorry, but I'm not really a farmer. You'll have to find someone else.

steps.text: 'I am sad to hear that, [player name/fremennik name], but you must do what you think is right.'

steps.player: I'm sorry, but I'm not really a diplomat. You'll have to find someone else.

steps.text: 'I am sad to hear that, [player name/fremennik name], but you must do what you think is right.'

options.text: Don't tell me, there's an anthem involved?
options.condition: If Throne of Miscellania has been completed:

steps.player: Don't tell me, there's an anthem involved?

steps.text: 'Your words are not clear to me. But please, try to find a way to bring our people closer together again.'

crisis-using-the-mud-on-the-tree-returni.prompt: Do you wish to return to shore?

steps.text: With a lot of effort you manage to get back to shore.

crisis-using-the-mud-on-the-tree-attempt.text: What a terrible stench! No one can live there, so you decide not to go either.

crisis-speaking-with-ragnar-again.speaker: Ragnar
crisis-speaking-with-ragnar-again.text: Really? You found her? Where is she, tell me!

crisis-speaking-with-ragnar-again.player: Well... there's something you should know.

crisis-speaking-with-ragnar-again.speaker: Ragnar
crisis-speaking-with-ragnar-again.text: What? Do not say such things! Tell me where you saw her!

crisis-speaking-with-ragnar-again.player: I didn't actually see her, not as such. But I did talk to her, right there, on that island in the center of the pool.

crisis-speaking-with-ragnar-again.speaker: Ragnar
crisis-speaking-with-ragnar-again.text: That island is bare! There's no one there! Do not try to deceive me, outerlander, she is not dead and you did not talk to her!

hamal-the-chieftain.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
hamal-the-chieftain.text: Where is she? Tell me, outerlander!

hamal-the-chieftain.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
hamal-the-chieftain.text: Do not play games with me. I gave you leave to walk about our camp, not to trick us.

steps.player: Never mind.
About the people of Rellekka...

options.text: Why do you hate them so much?

steps.player: Why do you hate them so much?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: We do not hate them, outerlander, but we do not approve of their ways either.

steps.player: But don't you basically believe in the same things?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: It is true that our beliefs are not all that different, but we have a different way of applying them, a stricter way.

steps.player: So you've never considered, say, making peace with them?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: We are not at war with them, outerlander, but we try to ignore each other.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: But I must admit that I have, in fact, sent out a representative to Rellekka to talk about improving relations and perhaps setting up a basic trade route.

steps.player: Great! Well, that was easy.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Unfortunately we have not heard from Svidi, our representative, for a few days.

steps.player: Shall I go looking for him as well then?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Do as you wish, outerlander.

options.text: You're all such a group of petty bickerers!
options.condition: If Throne of Miscellania has been completed

steps.player: You're all such a group of petty bickerers! I've only just gone and made peace between Miscellania and Etceteria!

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Miscellania? So that group survived?

steps.player: Why, do you know them?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Oh yes... that group left the mainland a long time ago. And good riddance to them, I say.

steps.player: Don't tell me you're fighting them as well.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Oh, we're not fighting anyone. But we cannot forgive them for their insulting behaviour before they left.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: It is quite inappropriate to pray to the gods when the moon is half full. Yet it is almost as if they wanted to make a point of it, holding parties in honour of gods almost every night.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: That, and they like to dress up in fancy clothes a bit too much to our tastes.

steps.player: Go on then, go on, tell me, who else split off from your little group of infighting barbarians?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: How do you mean? There is no one else. Well, there's the Gunnarian people who left this area over a century ago, but they don't really count, do they?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: And I suppose that the people of-

steps.player: No! Forget it! I didn't really want to hear all that!
About your food supplies...
From what I understand you're starting to run out?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Where did you get that idea from, outerlander?

steps.player: Er, I just happened to overhear it.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: There is some truth to it, yes. If it were not for my missing daughter, we would have moved on already, and finding food would be easier again for a while.

steps.player: Can I help you with finding a new supply of food?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: I would be interested to see how you would manage that, outerlander. But if you insist on trying, go ahead.

making-peace-leaving-the-mountain-camp.speaker: Guard
making-peace-leaving-the-mountain-camp.text: Go, outerlander, and do not hurry back.

making-peace-svidi.player: Are you, by any chance, Svidi? Sent by Hamal to talk to Brundt and the council of Rellekka?

making-peace-svidi.speaker: Svidi
making-peace-svidi.text: Maybe... who is asking? You're an outerlander, aren't you?

making-peace-svidi.player: Yes, but Hamal asked me to rescue you from a Rellekka prison. What are you doing here?

making-peace-svidi.speaker: Svidi
making-peace-svidi.text: I haven't actually been in Rellekka yet...

making-peace-svidi.player: Why, can't you find the way?

making-peace-svidi.speaker: Svidi
making-peace-svidi.text: Well, I'm not actually sure if I should go in there, you see.

making-peace-svidi.speaker: Svidi
making-peace-svidi.text: I've always been told that the people of Rellekka are ignorants, almost as bad as other outerlanders. I think they might kill me if I go there.

making-peace-svidi.player: Nonsense. I'm an outerlander and I haven't killed you either!

making-peace-svidi.speaker: Svidi
making-peace-svidi.text: Yes, but you're on your own, they have a whole village.

making-peace-svidi.speaker: Svidi
making-peace-svidi.text: So I don't want to go in there, but I don't want to go back to the camp and tell Hamal that I didn't dare to go to Rellekka either.

options.text: Aren't you supposed to be a ferocious warrior?

steps.player: Aren't you supposed to be a ferocious warrior?

steps.speaker: Svidi
steps.text: Not all of us are warriors.

steps.speaker: Svidi
steps.text: Some of us are schooled in the fine art of diplomacy.

options.text: Can't I persuade you to go in there somehow?

steps.player: Can't I persuade you to go in there somehow?

steps.speaker: Svidi
steps.text: I won't go in there unless I know it's safe.

steps.player: Do you want me to go with you as your bodyguard?

steps.speaker: Svidi
steps.text: You? But you're an outerlander! You'd probably lead me to a cave to kill me yourself!

steps.player: What if I get you some kind of guarantee of safe passage from the village? Will that do?

steps.speaker: Svidi
steps.text: Hmmmm...

steps.speaker: Svidi
steps.text: Yes, that will do.

making-peace-talking-to-svidi-before-rec.player: Weren't you on your way to Rellekka?

making-peace-talking-to-svidi-before-rec.speaker: Svidi
making-peace-talking-to-svidi-before-rec.text: Weren't you on your way to get me a guarantee of safe passage into Rellekka?
If the player hasn't talked with Brundt:

steps.player: Oh yes, I almost forgot.

making-peace-talking-to-svidi-before-rec.text: If the player has talked with Brundt:

steps.player: Brundt doesn't want to talk to any representative until your tribe gives back some rock or other.

steps.speaker: Svidi
steps.text: In that case I'm staying right here. I don't have the authority to trade away our rock.

steps.speaker: Svidi
steps.text: Besides, it's ours and he can't have it.

steps.player: The chieftain from the mountain camp has sent a representative to Rellekka!

steps.text: If the player is a Fremennik:
If the player is an outlander:

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Very unusual, outerlander, but we have not seen him yet.

steps.player: Well, that's the problem, he doesn't dare to come into Rellekka. He's afraid he's going to get hurt.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: What? He's not much of a warrior, is he?

steps.player: That's what I thought. He says he wants a guarantee of safety.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: I will meet with this man on one condition, outerlander.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: When their group split off from Rellekka, they stole one of the ancient relics of the Fremennik. Our ancient rock.

steps.player: Ancient rock? What did it do?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Do?

options.text: Did it contain vast magical powers?

steps.player: Did it contain vast magical powers?

options.text: Did it give the owner unimaginable strength?

steps.player: Did it give the owner unimaginable strength?

options.text: Was it the eternal prison of an immortal demon?

steps.player: Was it the eternal prison of an immortal demon?

steps.text: If The Fremennik Trials has been completed:

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Amusing, [Fremennik name], but as a Fremennik yourself you know better than that.
If The Fremennik Trials hasn't been completed:

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: No, no, no. Little do you understand our ways, outerlander.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: The rock was just that, a rock. It had no special properties and was in essence no different from any other rock.

steps.player: So what did it mean?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: It symbolised our refusal to use the runestones for ourselves, instead relying on our own abilities.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: The people you speak of took the stone with them when they left for the mountains. They claimed their way of living was more pure and closer to nature.

steps.player: And is that true?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Maybe, but where's the harm in a bit of feasting from time to time?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: In any case, before the council and I meet with anyone from their camp, they will have to give our rock back.

steps.player: Did it look pretty?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Hmm, not especially I think...

making-peace-talking-to-brundt-before-re.player: Why won't you meet with the representative of the mountain camp?

making-peace-talking-to-brundt-before-re.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
making-peace-talking-to-brundt-before-re.text: Like I said, we don't want anything to do with them until they give back our ancient rock.

making-peace-returning-into-the-camp-thr.speaker: Guard
making-peace-returning-into-the-camp-thr.text: I suppose I might as well let you pass now, since I can't seem to stop you anyway.

making-peace-returning-into-the-camp-thr.speaker: Guard
making-peace-returning-into-the-camp-thr.text: Just remember that I'm watching you.

steps.player: About the people of Rellekka...
Chieftain Brundt says that he won't meet with Svidi unless you give him back some rock or other.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: What, do you mean our ancient rock that our fathers took with them when they left the ignorants of Rellekka?

steps.player: Yes, that's the one.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Out of the question. That rock belongs to us. It symbolises what we stand for. What would Brundt want with it anyway?

steps.player: So I can't persuade you to part with the rock?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Did you not hear me the first time, outerlander? It belongs to us, we will not part with it.

making-peace-removing-the-half-a-rock-fr.text: You go into the peculiar looking tent.
You take a look around and see none of the camp dwellers about...
With a few swings of your pick, you split off a part of the rock and sneakily put it in your pocket.
If the player already has a half a rock:

steps.text: While two halves make one whole, it's better to just have half a rock.

making-peace-removing-the-half-a-rock-fr.text: Trying to obtain half a rock while the Ancient Rock is split:

steps.text: Someone else just had the same idea!

making-peace-exiting-tent-with-half-a-ro.speaker: Guard
making-peace-exiting-tent-with-half-a-ro.text: What do you have there, outerlander? It's not our rock, is it?

making-peace-exiting-tent-with-half-a-ro.player: No, of course not! See? It's a completely different rock, it's much smaller.

making-peace-exiting-tent-with-half-a-ro.speaker: Guard
making-peace-exiting-tent-with-half-a-ro.text: Alright, you be on your way then.

steps.player: I've brought you back your rock!

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Really? Let me see!
Player gives half a rock to Brundt

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: This rock seems a lot smaller than our bard made it out to be.

steps.player: Well, it's not the whole rock, it's part of the rock...
I split it in two.

steps.text: If the player is a Fremennik:

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: You truly have the Fremennik spirit in you, [player name]
If the player is an outlander:

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: You are unusually insightful for an outerlander!

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Yes, we are satisfied with sharing the rock. I'll meet with this representative and will inform the council to join us here in the longhall.
If The Fremennik Trials has been completed:

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Although I see that Manni is already here.

steps.player: Can I have that guarantee of safe passage, then, to give to the representative?

steps.text: If The Fremennik Trials hasn't been completed:

steps.player: Can I have that guarantee of safe passage, then, to give to the representative?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Oh yes, here it is.
a safety guarantee

making-peace-returning-to-svidi-with-the.player: Brundt gave me the guarantee of safe passage to give to you!

making-peace-returning-to-svidi-with-the.speaker: Svidi
making-peace-returning-to-svidi-with-the.text: Let me see that, I want to be sure it's authentic.
Player gives the safety guarantee to Svidi

making-peace-returning-to-svidi-with-the.speaker: Svidi
making-peace-returning-to-svidi-with-the.text: Okay, this looks valid enough. I'll go and talk to Brundt.

steps.player: I did it, I persuaded Brundt to speak to your representative!

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Indeed, outerlander, and how did you accomplish that without giving him our rock?

steps.player: Well, yeah, I need to talk to you about that...

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Worry not, you made a wise decision and your boldness is impressive.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: It does not matter, after all, how large the rock is, or what its shape is. And perhaps the two halves of the rock will have extra symbolism now, representing the two halves of the Fremennik culture.
If the safety guarantee hasn't been given to Svidi:

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: But first things first. Did Svidi go into Rellekka yet, to speak to Brundt on behalf of our tribe?

steps.player: Oops, I completely forgot about that. I'd better hurry back to him.

steps.text: If the safety guarantee has been given to Svidi:

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: I understand that Svidi's meeting with Brundt went quite well. I must thank you for your assistance, outerlander.

finding-food-talking-to-hamal-before-obt.player: I'm looking for some bushes that carry White Pearl fruit. Do you know where I can find any?

finding-food-talking-to-hamal-before-obt.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
finding-food-talking-to-hamal-before-obt.text: Weren't you the one who was supposed to be looking for it for me?

finding-food-talking-to-jokul.speaker: Jokul
finding-food-talking-to-jokul.text: Times are hard here at the moment. We've been here for too long and there is not much food left, or places where I can take my goats.

finding-food-talking-to-jokul.player: Well, I'm trying to find a new supply of food for your people. Any ideas on where to start?

finding-food-talking-to-jokul.speaker: Jokul
finding-food-talking-to-jokul.text: If only it were so easy!

finding-food-talking-to-jokul.speaker: Jokul
finding-food-talking-to-jokul.text: I have heard there is a certain kind of fruit... that will grow even here, in the mountains.

finding-food-talking-to-jokul.player: What's the name of the fruit?

finding-food-talking-to-jokul.speaker: Jokul
finding-food-talking-to-jokul.text: It is called White Pearl, named after its white appearance.

finding-food-talking-to-jokul.player: Any ideas on where to find some?

finding-food-talking-to-jokul.speaker: Jokul
finding-food-talking-to-jokul.text: I do not know. I believe it grows mainly in the mountains, and it can grow in even the most difficult circumstances.

finding-food-talking-to-jokul.speaker: Jokul
finding-food-talking-to-jokul.text: We cannot move on until we find the chieftain's daughter, and we do not generally move far inland. But perhaps you can search for it.

finding-food-talking-to-jokul.player: I'll see what I can find.

finding-food-talking-to-jokkul-again.player: Where could I find that fruit again?

finding-food-talking-to-jokkul-again.speaker: Jokul
finding-food-talking-to-jokkul-again.text: I do not know, outerlander, but you might want to try looking on mountains.

finding-food-talking-to-jokkul-again.speaker: Jokul
finding-food-talking-to-jokkul-again.text: No, if it grew on here I would have known.

finding-food-obtaining-the-white-pearl-s.text: If the player has appropriate gloves on:

steps.text: Your gloves protect you from the thorns as you pick the White Pearl fruit.

finding-food-obtaining-the-white-pearl-s.text: If the player doesn't have appropriate gloves on:

steps.text: Ouch! You just stuck your hand into some very sharp thorns.

finding-food-obtaining-the-white-pearl-s.text: If the player already has a white pearl:

steps.text: No need, you already have one of these.
You eat the White Pearl and spit out the seed when you're done. Mmm, tasty.

finding-food-obtaining-the-white-pearl-s.text: Getting another white pearl after eating it:

steps.text: You're content with having the seed of the fruit.

finding-food-obtaining-the-white-pearl-s.text: Trying to pick up a seed off the floor when you already have one:

steps.text: One seed should be enough.

finding-food-talking-to-jokul-after-obta.player: Look, I found the White Pearl fruit!

finding-food-talking-to-jokul-after-obta.speaker: Jokul
finding-food-talking-to-jokul-after-obta.text: You seem to be quite resourceful, outerlander. Go and show it to the chieftain.

steps.text: If the player has the white pearl:

steps.player: Here, I have something that might interest you.
It's White Pearl fruit, which grows in even the hardiest circumstances. I found this growing on White Wolf Mountain.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: And what use is one piece of fruit to us, outerlander? It won't feed our tribe for even a day.

steps.player: Oops, I hadn't thought of that.

steps.text: If the player has the white pearl seed:

steps.player: I've found this seed that may be of interest to you.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Interesting, what is it?

steps.player: It's the seed of the White Pearl fruit. It grows on White Wolf mountain, even in the snow.
With luck, you'll be able to grow it here as well.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: This is a great gift, [player name/fremennik name], which I humbly accept.
Player gives the white pearl seed to Hamal

finding-food-talking-to-jokul-after-givi.speaker: Jokul
finding-food-talking-to-jokul-after-givi.text: I must thank you for your generous gift, outerlander.

finding-food-talking-to-jokul-after-givi.speaker: Jokul
finding-food-talking-to-jokul-after-givi.text: Yes, the seed of the White Pearl. It grows remarkably well.

finding-food-talking-to-jokul-after-givi.player: Ah... well, glad to be of help.

finding-food-talking-to-hamal-before-fig.player: Hamal, I'm sorry, but your daughter is dead.

finding-food-talking-to-hamal-before-fig.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
finding-food-talking-to-hamal-before-fig.text: I told you before not to say such things.

finding-food-talking-to-hamal-before-fig.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
finding-food-talking-to-hamal-before-fig.text: What proof of it do you have anyway?

finding-food-talking-to-hamal-before-fig.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
finding-food-talking-to-hamal-before-fig.text: Then do not say it again. I appreciate what you've done for us already, but don't try our patience.

fighting-the-kendal-shining-pool.player: Hey, ehm... Asleif spirit thing? Hello?
I did what you asked me to! I improved the relations between Rellekka and the mountain camp, and I found a new supply of food!

fighting-the-kendal-shining-pool.text: 'Yes, [player name/fremennik name], I can sense that this is so.'

fighting-the-kendal-shining-pool.player: So do you have any other quests for me, perhaps with some bigger rewards?

fighting-the-kendal-shining-pool.text: 'I do not fully understand what you speak of, but I do have one more task I would like you to do.'
'My father does not believe that I am dead. In his heart, he knows it to be true, but he cannot accept it.'
'You must convince him, [player name/fremennik name]. Once you have convinced my father, everyone else in the camp will follow him. Then, perhaps, they can move on again.'

fighting-the-kendal-shining-pool.player: How do I do that, exactly? I don't think I'll be able to get him down to this little island.

fighting-the-kendal-shining-pool.text: 'I must leave that to you. All I know is that I was attacked by some creature or animal while I was sitting by the lake. It dragged me off and I remember nothing else.'
'Perhaps this will help you, I cannot provide further assistance.'

fighting-the-kendal-entering-the-cave.text: You take a very deep breath...

fighting-the-kendal-the-kendal-attacking.speaker: The Kendal
fighting-the-kendal-the-kendal-attacking.text: Do not attack me, puny mortal [player name/fremennik name]!

fighting-the-kendal-the-kendal-trying-to.speaker: The Kendal
fighting-the-kendal-the-kendal-trying-to.text: I did not give you permission to touch that, mortal!
This bear has no quarrel with you.

fighting-the-kendal-the-kendal-talking-t.speaker: The Kendal
fighting-the-kendal-the-kendal-talking-t.text: Who dares to disturb my slumber?

options.text: It's just me, no one special.

steps.player: It's just me, [player name/fremennik name], no one special.

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: Have you come, then, to pay your respects?

steps.player: How... exactly do I do that?

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: With your blood, mortal!

steps.player: Time to go, see you later!

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: Go now, mortal, but I'll be watching you!

steps.player: You mean a sacrifice? Are you some kind of god?

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: I am the guardian of the mountain, the god of the northern lands. I move the earth and control the skies. I am the Kendal!

options.text: I seek your advice, oh great one!

steps.player: I seek your advice, oh great one.
I seek the cowardly murderer of a young lady of a nearby clan of mountain people. Do you know where I can find this person?

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: I am not here to answer questions of such trivial nature! Go now before doom befalls you, mortal!

options.text: You look like you escaped from a fairground!

steps.player: You look like you escaped from a fairground!

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: I would not say such things if I were you, mortal!

options.text: You look like a man in a bearsuit!

steps.player: You look like a man in a bearsuit!

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: What did you say, mortal?

steps.player: I said, you look like a man wearing a bearsuit!

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: How did you figure that out? How did you know?

steps.player: I just said you looked like a man wearing a bearsuit, I didn't know you were!

steps.text: Conversation will resume from here if aborted

steps.player: So what are you doing here, pretending to be a god?

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: Ah, the people that live in the mountains here, they are a superstitious lot. They fear few things, but magic and gods they're scared to death of.

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: So I took on the guise of one of their legends. It's a good way of being left alone.

steps.player: And do you leave them alone as well?

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: Ah, you're referring to the skeletons you see here? Yes, I did. Most of the time, at least. When there was no troll to be ambushed, and I had to eat...

steps.player: Did you kill a young lady, by the lake? Just recently?

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: Recently? Oh no, the entrance you came through has been blocked off for a good many years now. I've only seen trolls and the occasional stray dwarf since then, until you came along.

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: But yes, more than ten years ago, I did kill someone like that.

options.text: Oh, never mind then, that can't be right.

steps.player: Oh, never mind then, that can't be the person I'm looking for. I'll be off.
Can I see that corpse? I'd like to make sure of something.

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: She is just over there, in the centre, with the dress. I did not eat her after I killed her, she was too beautiful for that.

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: I felt sorry for killing her, but by then it was already too late.

steps.player: Yes, she does match the description I was given, it is her after all!

options.text: Hand the body over to me!

steps.player: I demand that you hand the body over to me! I must return them to her father!

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: You demand nothing! You may have uncovered my disguise, but my claws can still tear you apart at will!

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: I will not allow you to leave!
The Kendal attacks the player

options.text: I humbly request to be given the remains.

steps.player: I humbly request to be given the remains, so I can return them to her father.

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: I cannot do that. If they knew I wasn't a god, and if her father knew I killed his daughter, the whole tribe would come in here at once and I'd be finished.

steps.player: I will kill you myself!

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: Come and try!
The Kendal attacks the player

options.text: Never mind then, I'd better leave

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: I'm afraid I can't allow you to leave either. You cannot tell anyone about me.
The Kendal attacks the player

steps.player: I think you're completely mad, walking around in your silly bearsuit, killing innocent people!

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: And how is that very much different from you, walking around in silly suits of armour, killing everything that moves?

steps.player: Never mind.

options.text: It's me, of whom many legends are sung.

steps.player: It's [player name/fremennik name], of whom many legends are sung.

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: You are brave, to come into my cave and say a thing like that!

options.text: Slumber? You didn't seem to be sleeping.

steps.player: Slumber? You didn't seem to be sleeping.

steps.speaker: The Kendal
steps.text: Do not mock me, mortal!

fighting-the-kendal-the-kendal-killing-t.text: You collect the helmet from the corpse of the 'bear' as a trophy.

fighting-the-kendal-the-kendal-trying-to.text: This must be someone else's corpse, you already have Asleif's corpse.
You'd better bring this back to the chieftain instead.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-be.player: I found the man who murdered Asleif! He was in a cave just by the pool, but I killed him!

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-be.speaker: Ragnar
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-be.text: Do not say such things, outerlander! She is not dead, merely missing.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-be.speaker: Ragnar
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-be.text: She'll show up again... yes, yes, I'm sure of it.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-be.player: But she's been missing for more than ten years!

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-be.speaker: Ragnar
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-be.text: Yes, I know... well, that doesn't mean she can't still come back, right?
If the player doesn't have the corpse:

steps.player: Er, yeah, right... sure.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-be.text: If the player has the corpse:

steps.player: Look, here, I even have her corpse!

steps.speaker: Ragnar
steps.text: I do not want to see any of the corpses you're carrying around with you! Begone!

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-shining-p.player: I found him! I found your murderer! It was some bear-like man who called himself the Kendal.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-shining-p.text: 'The Kendal is an ancient spirit of our people, but he is benevolent. Are you sure of this?'

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-shining-p.player: Well, it was actually a guy in a bearsuit. But he's dead now.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-shining-p.text: 'Go then, to my father, and show him what you've learned.'

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.player: Do you know there is a strange bear like thing in a cave near the pool?
Only the cave is hidden behind some trees, you see-
What, you mean you know that already?

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.text: Of course. We planted the trees there ourselves many years ago.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.text: It is unwise to come too close to a god, so we made sure no one would go there anymore.

options.text: And why didn't you tell me your daughter's been missing for years?

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.player: He's not a god! He's a man in a bearsuit! And he killed your daughter!
And why didn't you tell me she's been missing for more than ten years?

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.text: Fourteen years, to be exact. And I didn't say otherwise, did I? As for the Kendal, what proof have you of these serious accusations?
If the player hasn't defeated Kendal:

steps.player: You want proof for everything, don't you? Why don't you just go and have a look?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Like I said, it is not wise to approach a god so closely.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.text: If the player defeated Kendal but isn't wearing the bear mask:

steps.player: Well... I've only gone and killed him, haven't I?

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.text: If the player defeated Kendal and is wearing the bear mask:

steps.player: Well... I've only gone and killed him, haven't I? Look, I'm even wearing his silly hat!

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.text: You have? Then we made an enormous mistake.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.text: As did he. Impersonating a god bears the highest penalty imaginable, but I did not think that kind of justice would be delivered by the hand of an outerlander.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.player: I also found your daughter. The bearman killed her.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.text: So it is true then, after all? Let me see her body please.
If the player doesn't have the corpse:

steps.player: I didn't bring it with me, I'll go and look for it.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-abo.text: If the player has the corpse:

steps.player: Of course.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Yes, I see it is her. So it is also true that you spoke to her spirit at the pool?

steps.player: Yes, it's true.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Then she must be buried there, on the island at the center of the pool... to bring peace to her spirit. This is a most unusual situation, but will you bury her, [player name/fremennik name]?

steps.player: I will.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Then please listen closely. If she is given a proper burial, she is to be buried with some of her possessions. I see she's still wearing her dress, so you will need one more item.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: When she has been buried, you must build a cairn on top. It is our tradition to build these cairns in the shape of our longboats that we use when we need to cross the seas. You can use rocks for this purpose, about five or so should be enough.

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Only then are the burial rites complete.

steps.player: So I need to bury her with one of her possessions, and build a cairn on top made out of rocks. So where do I get another one of her possessions?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: Asleif had little possessions in life and none that have survived the years. I do not know where you might find such a thing, but perhaps Ragnar does, out by the pool.

steps.player: I won't.
I... ehm...
Errr...
I will.
I killed the bearman! He really was just a man after all, like I said!

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: You have? Then we made an enormous mistake.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-hamal-aga.text: If the player hasn't defeated Kendal:

steps.player: I need some help with killing this bear thing in the cave. Do you have any warriors to come with me?

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: If you wish to confront the god it is your own affair, outerlander, but we will not be any part of it.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-ag.speaker: Ragnar
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-ag.text: I heard the news from Hamal, outerlander. Alas, I have known this had to be so for a long time, but Hamal just didn't want to listen.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-ag.player: Well, Hamal asked me to bury her with some of her possessions. But he doesn't have any anymore.
Do you have anything that may help?

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-ag.speaker: Ragnar
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-ag.text: I'm not altogether sure... I do have one thing that may be appropriate.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-ag.speaker: Ragnar
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-ag.text: I was going to give her a necklace, when we were supposed to meet here many years ago.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-ag.speaker: Ragnar
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-ag.text: I still have it, and since it was a gift for Asleif, technically it's hers.

fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-ag.speaker: Ragnar
fighting-the-kendal-talking-to-ragnar-ag.text: Take it, outerlander, and bury it with her. It will be my parting gift.

options.text: Thank you. I will make sure she's given a proper burial now.
You've been waiting to give it to her all that time?

steps.player: You've been waiting to give it to her all that time?

steps.speaker: Ragnar
steps.text: Oh yes... she is my only love, you see, and will be so forever.

steps.player: But that's ridiculous! Don't you ever go out and have some fun? What is wrong with you people!

steps.speaker: Ragnar
steps.text: I do not expect you to understand such things. But perhaps you will find your own love one day, and then you will remember these words.
If Throne of Miscellania has been completed:

fighting-the-kendal-listening-to-the-shi.player: I convinced your father about your death. He asked me to give you a proper burial, here on this island.

fighting-the-kendal-listening-to-the-shi.text: 'Then my father made a wise decision. Please proceed.'

fighting-the-kendal-listening-to-the-shi.player: Well, it's kind of awkward... can you maybe be silent while I bury you?
Oh, right. Well, I'd better get on with it then.

fighting-the-kendal-laying-asleif-to-res.text: If the player does not have Asleif's necklace:

steps.text: She needs to be buried with some of her possessions, like jewelry.

fighting-the-kendal-laying-asleif-to-res.text: If the player has Asleif's necklace:

steps.text: You dig a hole in the ground, then carefully lay down the skeleton of the chieftain's daughter, together with her necklace. You then close the hole, creating a small burial mound. Now all you need to do is build a cairn on top.

fighting-the-kendal-listening-to-the-shi.player: Burying her must have really helped! I should get on with building the cairn on top.

fighting-the-kendal-listening-to-the-shi.text: If the player doesn't have enough muddy rocks:

steps.text: You don't have enough rocks to build a cairn. You need [x] more rock(s).

fighting-the-kendal-listening-to-the-shi.text: If the player has enough muddy rocks:

steps.text: You think you can hear a soft 'thank you' as the singing quietens down.

talking-to-hamal-after-quest-completion.text: If The Fremennik Trials has been completed:

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: You are a most unusual outerlander. The council of Rellekka was wise to make you an honourary Fremennik.

talking-to-hamal-after-quest-completion.text: If The Fremennik Trials has been completed and the requirements are met:

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: You are a most unusual outerlander. Perhaps you should seek to become an honourary Fremennik, in Rellekka.

talking-to-hamal-after-quest-completion.text: If The Fremennik Trials hasn't been completed the requirements are met:

steps.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
steps.text: You are a most unusual outerlander. I'm sure that you will be able to complete your Fremennik trials some time.

talking-to-hamal-after-quest-completion.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
talking-to-hamal-after-quest-completion.text: You have my thanks, in any case.

talking-to-hamal-after-quest-completion.player: So what are you all going to do now? Are you finally going to move to another location?

talking-to-hamal-after-quest-completion.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
talking-to-hamal-after-quest-completion.text: No, I've decided to set up a permanent camp here.

talking-to-hamal-after-quest-completion.speaker: Hamal the Chieftain
talking-to-hamal-after-quest-completion.text: There is no need to move now with our new supply of food. Also, there is a protective spirit looking after us now.

options.text: Excuse me, have you seen my helmet?
Well, I must be off again.
What exactly happened to your daughter?
I thought you didn't believe in magic?
